story: As a platform engineer, I want to ship a notebook template whose panel renders with no import the researcher types, so that the end user only ever clicks
outcome: the end user only ever clicks

story: As a researcher, I want to paste a one-line cell into an existing notebook, so that I can add the panel without starting over from the template
outcome: I can add the panel without starting over from the template

story: As a researcher, I want profile and queue dropdowns populated from the TauCluster, so that I pick platform policy instead of typing it
outcome: I pick platform policy instead of typing it

story: As a researcher, I want to see which profile and queue were resolved and why, so that I trust the defaults rather than guessing
outcome: I trust the defaults rather than guessing

story: As a researcher, I want each offered profile to say whether a notebook running in its own kernel gets a GPU, so that I am not surprised by a silent CPU fallback
outcome: I am not surprised by a silent CPU fallback

story: As a researcher, I want to pick companion files sitting beside the notebook, so that the run carries what it imports
outcome: the run carries what it imports

story: As a researcher, I want the picker to bound what it reads and refuse an oversized file with a reason, so that a large file cannot exhaust the notebook server
outcome: a large file cannot exhaust the notebook server

story: As a researcher, I want the panel to resolve the notebook I am working in and package it with a runner, so that the notebook itself is the job
outcome: the notebook itself is the job

story: As a researcher, I want unsupported notebook shapes refused with a reason, so that I never get a silently wrong job
outcome: I never get a silently wrong job

story: As a researcher, I want the panel to render a ray.io/v1 RayJob with Kueue's admission contract intact, so that submitting still enters fair-share queueing
outcome: submitting still enters fair-share queueing

story: As a researcher, I want the work that needs a GPU to execute where the GPUs are, so that a notebook doing its own CUDA training does not silently fall back to CPU
outcome: a notebook doing its own CUDA training does not silently fall back to CPU

story: As a platform engineer, I want the Python renderer to match the Go renderer for the same logical job, so that the plugin cannot drift from the CLI
outcome: the plugin cannot drift from the CLI

story: As a researcher, I want the panel to apply the workload and give a clear actionable error when the profile or queue is wrong, so that I know whether to fix my config or ask the platform owner
outcome: I know whether to fix my config or ask the platform owner

story: As a researcher, I want a dry-run that renders without applying, so that I can inspect the manifest before it consumes quota
outcome: I can inspect the manifest before it consumes quota

story: As a researcher, I want the resolved namespace, queue and profile echoed back after submit, so that I can confirm the platform applied the policy I expected
outcome: I can confirm the platform applied the policy I expected

story: As a researcher, I want a loss curve read from the run's house-format JSONL metrics, so that I can see convergence without leaving the notebook and without a second metrics pipeline
outcome: I can see convergence without leaving the notebook and without a second metrics pipeline

story: As a researcher, I want loss parsed from the job's stdout when no metrics file exists, so that a plain print statement is enough
outcome: a plain print statement is enough

story: As a researcher, I want the portal series API used as a fallback source, so that history remains readable after the run ends
outcome: history remains readable after the run ends

story: As a researcher, I want per-device GPU utilization with explicit observed flags, so that a real zero is distinguishable from a value that was never reported
outcome: a real zero is distinguishable from a value that was never reported

story: I want scrape coverage and framebuffer usage shown together, so that I can tell a partial scrape from a healthy one
outcome: I can tell a partial scrape from a healthy one

story: As a researcher, I want automatic polling with a visible interval and a stop control, so that the panel's updates are explainable
outcome: the panel's updates are explainable

story: As a researcher, I want a completed run to say that live GPU samples are gone, so that I am never shown a false zero
outcome: I am never shown a false zero

story: As a researcher, I want a link to the Ray dashboard for my run's cluster, so that I can drill into Ray without knowing the proxy URL scheme
outcome: I can drill into Ray without knowing the proxy URL scheme

story: As a researcher, I want the dashboard embedded only when it can actually load, so that I never stare at a blank frame with no error
outcome: I never stare at a blank frame with no error

story: As a researcher, I want the admission state and the Kueue message verbatim, so that I can tell waiting-for-quota apart from broken
outcome: I can tell waiting-for-quota apart from broken

story: As a researcher, I want the pod list with phase, node and restart count, so that I can spot a crash loop myself
outcome: I can spot a crash loop myself

story: As a researcher, I want diagnostics with severity, message and suggestion, so that a failure tells me what to do next
outcome: a failure tells me what to do next

story: As a researcher, I want the suggested next command rendered copy-pasteable, so that recovery does not require guessing
outcome: recovery does not require guessing

story: As a reviewer, I want a standalone HTML export of the panel, so that I can attach the run's evidence to a report or a pull request
outcome: I can attach the run's evidence to a report or a pull request

story: As a reviewer, I want a deep link into the portal experiment page, so that I can see the full run rather than a summary
outcome: I can see the full run rather than a summary

story: As a platform engineer, I want the plugin's scope documented as single-active-workspace with isolation explicitly a non-goal, so that nobody mistakes a path check for tenant isolation
outcome: nobody mistakes a path check for tenant isolation

story: As a tenant admin, I want to see which workspace, namespace and team a profile authorizes, so that I know who is entitled to it
outcome: I know who is entitled to it

story: As a tenant admin, I want only ready profiles offered from the cluster's resolved status catalog, so that a stale or unready profile cannot be selected
outcome: a stale or unready profile cannot be selected

story: As a tenant admin, I want profiles filtered by the namespace and team they authorize, so that the plugin cannot offer capacity a tenant is not entitled to
outcome: the plugin cannot offer capacity a tenant is not entitled to

story: As a platform engineer, I want the plugin's readiness and applicability rules to match the CLI and the portal, so that there is one authorization policy rather than three
outcome: there is one authorization policy rather than three

story: As a tenant admin, I want a submission refused when the profile does not apply, so that entitlement is enforced at the boundary rather than in a dropdown
outcome: entitlement is enforced at the boundary rather than in a dropdown

story: As a platform engineer, I want an auditable record of workspace and profile changes, so that access changes can be reviewed after the fact
outcome: access changes can be reviewed after the fact

story: As an MLOps engineer, I want the submitted run to carry a reproducibility record, so that I can rebuild the environment that produced a result
outcome: I can rebuild the environment that produced a result

story: As an MLOps engineer, I want the payload digest visible on the workload, so that I can confirm which notebook bytes actually ran
outcome: I can confirm which notebook bytes actually ran

story: As an MLOps engineer, I want the checkpoints and artifacts a run produced to be discoverable, so that a result can leave the notebook
outcome: a result can leave the notebook

story: As an MLOps engineer, I want to promote a checkpoint to a durable location, so that it survives the RayCluster being torn down
outcome: it survives the RayCluster being torn down

story: As an SRE, I want run lifecycle state visible after the RayCluster is torn down, so that I can tell what happened to a finished run
outcome: I can tell what happened to a finished run

story: I want the run's metrics history retained beyond the run, so that I can compare it against later runs
outcome: I can compare it against later runs

story: As an SRE, I want per-team cost attribution for the run, so that consumption can be charged to the team that caused it
outcome: consumption can be charged to the team that caused it
